items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I was in a thing with doing a clinic a year or so ago at UCLA with Kenny Burrell

ctx.x: Yeah this festival seems to be —

I don’t really — and I’ve traveled with Milt Hinton extensively and Milt is the most wonderful guy in the world and always very supportive. On a one-to-one basis I have never experienced it I’m happy to say. And I hope that it would be less and less as time goes on. Because I have experienced — I was in a thing with doing a clinic a year or so ago at UCLA with Kenny Burrell and guys were asking us questions, and this one guy kept saying, “Since jazz is an African-American art form, I mean where do you get off…
That’s a good point. And depending on what history writer you read, sometimes you’ll get that opinion and sometimes you won’t.
